title: Python OOP Basics Quiz
description: Test your understanding of Python's basic Object-Oriented Programming concepts: classes, objects, constructors, and methods.

questions.question:
What will be the output of the following code?

```python
class Person:
    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
p = Person('Alice')
print(p.name)
```
questions.explanation: The __init__ constructor initializes the attribute `name` with 'Alice'. So, p.name prints 'Alice'.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly defines a method in a class?
questions.explanation: In Python, a method inside a class must have `self` as its first parameter to access instance attributes.

questions.question: How do you create an object of a class `Car`?
questions.explanation: In Python, objects are created by calling the class like a function: `c = Car()`.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `__init__` method?
options: It initializes the object when it is created
questions.explanation: The `__init__` method is the constructor used to initialize instance attributes when a new object is created.

questions.question:
What will the following code print?

```python
class A:
    def greet(self):
        print('Hello')
obj = A()
obj.greet()
```
questions.explanation: The `greet` method of class A prints 'Hello'. obj.greet() calls this method.

questions.question: Which of the following adds an attribute `age` to an object `p` of class `Person`?
questions.explanation: Instance attributes are added to the object using dot notation: `p.age = 25`.

questions.question:
What will be the output of:

```python
class Test:
    def show(self):
        print('Test Method')
obj = Test()
obj.show()
```
questions.explanation: The show method prints 'Test Method'. Calling obj.show() executes it.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE about objects in Python?
options: Objects are instances of a class
Objects are the same as classes
questions.explanation: An object is a concrete instance of a class, which can have attributes and methods.

questions.question:
What will the following code print?

```python
class Sample:
    def __init__(self, x):
        self.x = x
s = Sample(10)
print(s.x)
```
questions.explanation: The __init__ method sets s.x = 10. So, print(s.x) outputs 10.

questions.question: Which of these correctly calls a method `display` of object `obj`?
questions.explanation: Methods are called on objects using dot notation: `obj.display()`.
